speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the specific movements you are experiencing, and when did they first start? Also, have you noticed any changes in your mood, memory, or sleep patterns recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your psychotic symptoms have improved, I want to focus on the movement disorder. Do you feel like you are moving involuntarily when you are trying to stay still, or do you experience stiffness and slowness of movement?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the description; those are classic signs of akathisia, a common side effect of your risperidone. How severe is this restlessness on a scale of 1 to 10, and does it significantly interfere with your daily activities or sleep? Also, have you noticed any muscle weakness, drooping eyelids, or blurred vision since starting the medication?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-induced akathisia secondary to risperidone. I recommend reducing the risperidone dose or switching to an antipsychotic with a lower risk of extrapyramidal symptoms.
